argument_summary: Certification is supportable only on a narrow, caveated reading of the existing record. The admissible evidence shows current aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports launch readiness overall. The same record also shows a current small-business onboarding regression 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold, so the defense cannot treat prior approval or an informal monitoring comment as substitutes for current-release treatment. The strongest compliant position is to certify on the basis of current aggregate readiness while explicitly documenting the small-business onboarding limitation in the current release packet and describing post-launch monitoring as supporting context only.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify this position. The policy argument stands on the existing admissible evidence without urgency framing.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not require denial whenever a segment weakness exists; it requires that current-release documentation reflect current evaluation results and that material segment weaknesses be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation. On the admissible record, prior approval is contextual only, and the release-thread monitoring comment is not approved mitigation or owner acceptance. Certification is therefore defensible only as caveated compliance tied to explicit current-release disclosure of the subgroup limitation.
concessions: The current small-business onboarding slice is below threshold and weakens the certification record.
The prior approved release cannot be treated as governance cover for the current release because the current regression arose after the retrieval configuration change and current eval batch.
The informal monitoring comment does not satisfy approved mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure requirements.
This is a thin certification record, so any clean-compliance characterization would overstate the evidence.
